After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding access to its new iPad interface, including a brand-new Mac-like sidebar. Here's what you need to know.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app interface

Although WhatsApp initially began adapting its iOS app for the major Liquid Glass visual overhaul last October, the company didn't bring the new design to the iPad until this June in a limited test.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the new design includes Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons, and contextual menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on iPhone.

The latest report from the site says WhatsApp is now rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the original bottom tab bar with a new Mac-like sidebar as the default layout.

This sidebar follows the layout already used in WhatsApp for Mac, giving users quick access to Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls, Meta AI, and other parts of the app. Users can also hide it to free up more space for the chat list and conversation view.

Here's the report:

WABetaInfo notes that the new sidebar is available to some testers using the latest TestFlight build, though some users on the regular App Store version are also starting to see it.

As is often the case with WhatsApp rollouts, the new interface may take some time to reach all users, whether they're on the beta or the official release. However, iPad users will benefit from a more tablet-appropriate layout once it arrives.
